messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC-2026 — embeddings-queue tail latency elevated. Alert triggered: embed-queue > 95th pct > 800ms for 10m. Possible customer impact: slow embeddings for some heavy customers and longer API tails for Hybrid routing users. See dashboard: https://observability.redwood/INC-2026

Samir: quick handoff — I'm wrapping up my shift, leaving a summary + current mitigations. Primary for next 6h: @Mira (primary). Secondary/backup: @Jules. If both out, page @Priya.

Samir: Current state — alerts are still firing but error rates are low. Root cause hypothesis: sudden surge of long sequences hitting prefetch + KV cache misses causing worker saturation. A few models (emb-small-v1) are queuing and causing backpressure into generator pool.

Samir: Active alerts and what they mean:
- embed-queue: high 95/99th latency (alerting)
- worker-oom: a couple of transient OOM restarts on embed-worker-3 (non-fatal, restart loop avoided)
- routing-fallback-rate: increased fallbacks to smaller-model for some routes (~3% of requests)

Samir: Mitigations already in progress (do NOT revert without approval):
1) Autoscale bump applied to embed-worker ASG from min=4 -> min=8 (manual bump). Visible in infra console.
2) Temporary prefetch throttle enabled for long-seq clients (config flag: prefetch.long_seq=false).
3) Enabled KV-cache aggressive TTL extension on hot partitions (approx +30s).
4) Canary fallback policy tightened to reduce noisy fallbacks to tiny-model for enterprise orgs (policy change pushed).

Samir: Commands used / useful checks:
```bash
# check pod restarts and CPU
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=embed-worker -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs embed-worker-3 --tail=200

# scale worker set (if needed)
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/embed-worker --replicas=12

# toggle prefetch gate (danger: may increase overall latency for small requests)
redwoodctl config set prefetch.long_seq false --env production
```

Samir: Observability links (copy-paste):
- Embeddings queue dashboard: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/embed-queue
- Per-org routing/fallbacks: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/routing-fallbacks
- Recent deploys: https://deploys.redwood/history (look for embed-worker releases in past 48h)

Samir: Customer impact notes — we saw two support tickets reporting ~5–10s delays for batch embedding jobs. No data loss. Most interactive calls are seeing 200–500ms extra latency; tail worse. Enterprise customers on dedicated pools are mostly fine (isolation).

Samir: Open action items for next shift:
- Watch for embed-worker OOM patterns. If the same pod restarts >3x in 15m, escalate to eng-runtime (pager).
- Validate that autoscale min increase settles (give it 10–15m) and monitor 95th pct. If still >700ms, scale further in +2 steps.
- If fallback-rate climbs >5%, rollback canary policy change and contact routing team.
- Confirm prefetch gate hasn't broken small-request latency (check p50/p90).

Samir: Escalation contacts:
- eng-runtime on-call (pager): +1-555-0133 (via PagerDuty)
- infra lead: Priya (DM or page)
- product contact (for customer comms): jen@redwood.com (if we need a status update)

Samir: Coverage gaps to note — between 02:00–03:00 UTC there is limited overlap with EMEA oncall. If the situation degrades during that window, please escalate early to Priya so we can spin additional capacity.

Jules: Quick q — do we have memory metrics for embed-worker pods? Samir, you mentioned OOMs but not sustained memory pressure.

Samir: yes — recent spikes coincide with a single tenant sending 200k token batched requests. Memory spiked but pods recovered after restart. Use: https://observability.redwood/metrics/embed-worker/memory?range=1h and filter by org_id.

Mira: taking primary. Thanks for notes Samir — I'll monitor the dashboards for the next 6h. My phone is on. If OOMs >3x I'll attempt a controlled restart of the problematic replica and annotate in this thread before doing it.

Mira: immediate plan: 1) confirm autoscale settled, 2) check fallback-rate window and org-level impacts, 3) run quick query to list top offending orgs.

Priya: I'm reachable if we need extra infra scaling beyond the ASG — I can spin up additional instances in the region manually. Also happy to coordinate customer comms if we need to warn any big orgs.

Jules: I'll own the runbook tasks. If Mira wants me to execute a scale, ping me and I'll run the kubectl scale command.

Samir: one more: don't forget to annotate the incident in the runbook when you make config changes — include timestamps and which flags were flipped. Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/embeddings-queue-incident.

incident-bot: Note: INC-2026 severity remains P2. Next automated reminder in 30m.

Mira: logged — first follow-up in 10m. I'll update thread with p95 numbers and list top 5 orgs causing load.

Jules: ack. I'll stand by for scale requests.

Priya: ack. I'll watch infra autoscaling events and be ready to intervene.

Samir: leaving now — ping me if you need context, but I may be slow after 10m. Good handoff everyone. :white_check_mark:
